newsitem.title: USA: Vishay bid for GI unit has unknowns - Analysts.
newsitem.headline: Vishay bid for GI unit has unknowns - Analysts.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology Corp's emergence as a possible bidder for General Instrument Corp's semiconductor unit received guarded approval from analysts, who noted Vishay's plans are thin on details.
Earlier, Vishay said it was one of several firms interested in acquiring Power Semiconductor, the power transistor unit that generated sales of $360 million in 1996.
"It does make sense," said Richard Jacobs, an analyst at Janney Montgomery Scott, of Vishay's possible acquisition move. "I think it's a positive thing...if it happens."
Jacobs maintains a buy rating on Vishay.
Vishay refused to elaborate on terms of a possible bid.

Analysts said Vishay's acquisition of the company will allow it to enter the $14 billion discrete semiconductor market with an established, profitable firm, and in doing so, will bolster its international presence.

"(The acquisition) would give them some manufacturing in the Far East, and (allow them to) sell a product to the same customers that they currently sell to," said Theodor Kundtz an analyst at Lehman Brothers.
General Instrument said that in 1996 about 70 percent of the semiconductor unit's sales were outside of the U.S.

Jim Feldham, president of Semico Research in Phoenix, said that power transistor firms, which use older technology in diverse applications sold to automotive, consumer and industrial manufacturers, are "cash cows" for some firms.
"They use older technology, and can use cheaper equipment," which are often fully depreciated, he said.

Stephen Madonna of Legg Mason Wood Walker said that Power Semiconductor appears to be very profitable, with sales growth near 10 to 11 percent a year and operating margins growth in the range of 23 to 24 percent.

But Feldham warned that any company interested in such an operation must walk into the deal knowing that it is a competitive business and that to succeed the buyer need be manufacturing-oriented and focused on production efficiencies.

Feldahm noted that Power Semiconductor ranks among the second tier in this field, after companies like Motorola Inc, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, NEC Corp, Hitachi Electronics Ltd, and International Rectifier.
Analysts also voiced concerns about Vishay's bid for the unit, noting that there still is no word on which other firms are competing, or how much the transaction would cost Vishay.
"There are a lot of unknowns," Kundtz said.
